high.title: Government Exempts Import Duties on Aircraft Spare Parts and LPG as Part of Economic Stimulus Package
high.summary: The Indonesian government has launched an economic stimulus package for H2-2026 through Ministry of Finance Regulation (PMK) No. 50/2026, setting 0% import duties on selected goods including aircraft MRO components and LPG used as petrochemical feedstock. The policy is a direct response to President Prabowo's directive to help businesses cope with rising production costs amid global economic pressures. This measure is significant for aviation and petrochemical industries as it directly reduces input costs and improves competitiveness.

high.title: US Imposes New 25% Tariffs on Brazil Covering Furniture, Ethanol, Machinery, and Other Commodities
high.summary: The United States plans to impose new 25% tariffs on Brazilian goods including furniture, ethanol, machinery, footwear, and sugar, effective July 22, marking Brazil as the first country targeted under Section 301 of the Trade Act of 1974 following the Supreme Court's February ruling that struck down Trump's broader emergency tariff regime. This development signals a renewed wave of US trade protectionism that could have spillover implications for Indonesian exporters if similar tariff actions are directed at other emerging markets. Indonesian investors should monitor whether comparable Section 301 investigations could be initiated against Indonesia's key export sectors.

high.title: Bitcoin Price Surges Past Rp 1.17 Billion
high.summary: Bitcoin has climbed back to US$ 65,500 (approximately Rp 1.17 billion), marking its highest level in five weeks. Other major cryptocurrencies also gained, with Ethereum at US$ 1,880, XRP at US$ 1.11, and Solana at US$ 75.80. The rally is driven by regulatory optimism, growing institutional investor interest, and broader global economic sentiment, signaling a potential recovery in crypto market confidence.

high.title: Antam Gold Price Rises Again to Rp 2,612,000 per Gram
high.summary: Antam 24-karat gold price increased by Rp 7,000 per gram to Rp 2,612,000, recovering after a sharp drop of Rp 35,000 per gram the previous day. Over the past week, prices have ranged between Rp 2,601,000 and Rp 2,640,000 per gram, while the monthly range sits between Rp 2,601,000 and Rp 2,670,000 per gram. This rebound is relevant for investors tracking safe-haven assets and commodity price trends in Indonesia.

high.title: Trump's New Tariffs Cause JCI to Plunge
high.summary: Indonesia's Jakarta Composite Index (JCI) fell 1.88% to 6,196.43 on Friday, July 24, 2026, driven by US President Donald Trump's imposition of new import tariffs of 10–12.5% on 60 trading partners, including Indonesia, alongside escalating Middle East tensions. The LQ45 blue-chip index also dropped 1.97%, with 587 stocks declining versus only 104 gaining. This marks a significant market-moving event as US trade policy directly impacts Indonesian exports and investor sentiment.

high.title: Indonesia Successfully Issues Debut Panda Bonds Worth 7 Billion Yuan, Orders Reach Rp 44 Trillion
high.summary: The Indonesian government issued its first-ever yuan-denominated Panda Bonds worth 7 billion yuan (approximately US$1.033 billion) on July 23, 2026, with 3-year and 5-year tenors. The issuance was overwhelmingly oversubscribed, with peak orderbook demand reaching 17 billion yuan (equivalent to ~Rp 44.95 trillion), signaling strong appetite from Chinese domestic investors. This landmark transaction diversifies Indonesia's sovereign debt financing base and strengthens economic ties with China.

high.title: Government Offers Tax Incentives in Indonesia International Financial Center (PFII), Valid for Up to 50 Years
high.summary: A draft bill for Indonesia's International Financial Center (PFII) reveals sweeping tax incentives for businesses operating within the zone, including income tax, VAT, luxury goods tax, and customs facilities for up to 50 years. The incentives apply to 18 categories of financial and investment service activities conducted by foreign tax subjects, with shorter durations for supporting businesses. This policy is designed to attract major international financial institutions and could significantly reshape Indonesia's financial landscape.

high.title: Tax Amnesty Participants Who Have Not Repatriated Assets to Face Tax Audits
high.summary: Finance Minister Purbaya Yudhi Sadewa announced stricter enforcement against tax amnesty participants who have not repatriated their overseas assets to Indonesia. The ministry will work with PPATK (Financial Intelligence Unit) to trace and audit all incoming funds linked to non-compliant taxpayers. This signals a significant shift from incentive-based encouragement to active enforcement, potentially affecting wealthy individuals and businesses with offshore assets.

high.title: 200 Rural Banks (BPR/BPRS) Queuing for Merger Approval at OJK
high.summary: As of June 2026, 200 Rural Banks (BPR/BPRS) are in the process of seeking merger approval from Indonesia's Financial Services Authority (OJK), with 81 already approved to consolidate into 24 entities. OJK's Head of Banking Supervision, Dian Ediana Rae, confirmed this is part of a national banking consolidation policy under POJK No. 7/2024. This large-scale consolidation wave is reshaping Indonesia's rural banking landscape and may impact credit access in regional markets.

high.title: Government Offers Tax Incentives in Indonesia International Financial Center (PFII) - Here Are the Details
high.summary: The newly enacted PFII (Indonesia International Financial Center) law grants sweeping tax incentives including income tax, VAT, luxury goods tax, and customs exemptions for businesses operating within the zone, applicable for up to 50 years. These facilities target 18 categories of financial and investment services conducted by foreign tax subjects, making PFII highly attractive to international capital. This represents a major structural shift in Indonesia's financial regulatory landscape with significant implications for foreign investment flows.

high.title: Not Relying on State Budget: Where Does the Initial Capital for PFII Come From?
high.summary: The PFII (Indonesia International Financial Center) law, officially passed on July 21, 2026, designates Danantara (BPI Daya Anagata Nusantara) as the primary source of initial capital for the PFII Management Institution (LP PFII), structured as a special investment. Additional funding sources include private entities, state/regional asset donations, and other legally permissible funding, indicating a deliberate effort to keep state budget exposure minimal. This directly implicates Danantara's investment strategy and signals the government's commitment to establishing Indonesia as a regional financial hub.

high.title: Foreign Capital of Rp 1.3 Trillion Exits Indonesian Capital Market
high.summary: Foreign investors recorded a net sell of Rp 1.36 trillion on Friday (24/7) as the IDX Composite (IHSG) weakened amid global uncertainty from new US tariffs and Middle East conflict. Cumulative net foreign selling throughout 2026 has nearly reached Rp 80 trillion, with year-to-date figures standing at Rp 79.09 trillion. This persistent foreign capital outflow signals significant pressure on Indonesian equities and warrants close monitoring by investors.

high.title: Asian Stock Markets Fall, IHSG Plunges Nearly 2%
high.summary: The IDX Composite (IHSG) dropped sharply by 1.75% to 6,204.63 during the first trading session on Friday (24/7), at one point falling over 2% to 6,161.13, in line with broad weakness across global markets. Trading volume reached 24.60 billion shares with a transaction value of Rp 10.51 trillion. The sharp decline reflects heightened global risk sentiment and poses immediate concerns for Indonesian equity investors.

high.title: Warning: Tax Amnesty Participants Who Have Not Repatriated Assets to Face Tax Audits
high.summary: Finance Minister Purbaya Yudhi Sadewa has announced plans to tighten oversight of Tax Amnesty and Voluntary Disclosure Program (PPS) participants who have not repatriated their overseas assets to Indonesia, involving the Financial Transaction Reports and Analysis Centre (PPATK). The government will conduct tax investigations on all incoming funds linked to non-compliant taxpayers. This enforcement shift could significantly impact wealthy individuals and businesses with undeclared offshore assets.

medium.title: Finance Minister Purbaya Imposes Anti-Dumping Duties on Duplex Paperboard from South Korea, Malaysia, and Taiwan
medium.summary: Indonesian Finance Minister Purbaya Yudhi Sadewa has issued PMK No. 40/2026 imposing anti-dumping duties on duplex paperboard imports from South Korea, Malaysia, and Taiwan, effective June 25, 2026 through 2031, following an investigation by Indonesia's Anti-Dumping Committee that confirmed dumping practices causing material injury to domestic industry. This five-year protective measure is relevant for domestic paper and packaging manufacturers who will benefit from reduced import competition, as well as downstream industries reliant on imported duplex paperboard who may face higher input costs.

medium.title: National Food Agency Denies Premium Rice Shortage, Acknowledges Price Increases
medium.summary: Indonesia's National Food Agency (Bapanas) has denied a shortage of premium rice in modern retail outlets, stating that supplies from state-owned enterprises including Bulog and ID Food brands remain available, though it acknowledged that prices have risen and are approaching the government-set maximum retail price (HET). The situation is noteworthy for food sector investors and FMCG retailers as supply inconsistencies across retail outlets and upward price pressure on premium rice could signal broader food inflation risks.

medium.title: Kopdes Merah Putih Village Cooperative Debt Repayments to State Banks Begin in September
medium.summary: Village cooperatives (Kopdes Merah Putih) that received credit facilities of up to Rp 3 billion each from state-owned banks (Himbara) will begin their first loan repayments in September 2026. Coordinating Minister for Food Zulkifli Hasan confirmed the first installment deadline falls in September, with repayments channeled through Agrinas Pangan. This is significant for state bank investors as it marks the start of credit performance monitoring for this large-scale government cooperative program.

medium.title: 4 Toll Roads Designated as Emergency Runways for Fighter Jets
medium.summary: The Indonesian government has designated four toll road sections — Banda Aceh-Sigli, Jakarta-Cikampek II South, Terbanggi Besar-Pematang Panggang-Kayu Agung, and Probolinggo-Banyuwangi — as emergency military runways for the Indonesian Air Force. The roads will continue to operate normally as toll roads under standard conditions. This reflects growing dual-use infrastructure investment and may be relevant for toll road operators and infrastructure investors monitoring government strategic asset utilization.

medium.title: Gold Prices Stagnant Despite Renewed Middle East Tensions — Here's Why
medium.summary: Despite renewed geopolitical tensions in the Middle East, gold prices remained largely flat during July 20–25, 2026, rising only Rp 2,000 per gram, a stark contrast to earlier surges that pushed prices above Rp 3 million per gram. An analyst attributed the stagnation to a shift in investor preference toward foreign currencies (forex) for short-term gains rather than gold as a safe-haven asset. This trend reflects changing retail investment behavior in Indonesia that could affect gold demand going forward.

medium.title: RANS Entertainment Director Grandy Prajayakti Resigns Shortly After IPO
medium.summary: PT Rans Entertainment Indonesia Tbk (RANS), the publicly listed company owned by celebrity Raffi Ahmad, announced the resignation of Director Grandy Prajayakti effective July 22, 2026, citing personal reasons. The resignation comes shortly after RANS completed its IPO earlier in July 2026, raising potential concerns among new investors about management stability. The company's finance director confirmed receipt of the resignation letter via an official disclosure to the Indonesia Stock Exchange.

medium.title: Food Commodity Prices Rise: Chicken Meat and Eggs Up, Red Chili Prices Also Climb
medium.summary: On Sunday July 26, 2026, key food commodities saw broad price increases according to Bank Indonesia's PIHPS data. Fresh chicken meat rose 1.69% to Rp 39,100/kg, eggs increased 1.02% to Rp 29,600/kg, and large red chili climbed 1.48% to Rp 48,150/kg. These price movements are relevant to Indonesia's inflation outlook and may influence Bank Indonesia's monetary policy considerations.

medium.title: Food Price Tracker: Beef, Rice, and Sugar Rise While Chili and Shallots Fall
medium.summary: As of July 5, 2026, staple food prices showed mixed movements with beef, rice, and sugar rising while chili and shallots declined sharply. Red chili fell the most at 7.93% to Rp 62,100/kg, and shallots dropped 6% to Rp 47,800/kg. These fluctuations in strategic food commodities are key indicators for Indonesia's monthly inflation data.

medium.title: Gold Prices Stagnant Despite Renewed Middle East Tensions - Here's Why
medium.summary: Antam 24-karat gold prices rose only Rp 2,000 per gram during the July 20-25, 2026 trading week despite escalating Middle East tensions, a stark contrast to previous periods when geopolitical risk drove prices above Rp 3 million per gram. Currency analyst Ibrahim Assuaibi attributes the muted response to a shift in investor behavior, with more Indonesians redirecting funds into foreign currencies (forex) for short-term gains rather than gold as a safe-haven asset. This trend has important implications for retail investors and commodity traders monitoring domestic gold market dynamics.

medium.title: Africa's Economy Threatened by Super El Niño, Potential Losses of Up to US$20 Billion
medium.summary: The African Development Bank warns that the Super El Niño phenomenon could slash GDP of the most affected African nations by 1-2%, translating to losses of US$10-20 billion continent-wide, with farmers already losing nearly US$330 million in income due to drought this year. The fisheries sector faces additional disruption from rising sea temperatures and storms. While centered on Africa, this development is relevant to Indonesian investors as El Niño conditions also affect Southeast Asia's agricultural output and global commodity prices.

medium.title: Meat and Rice Prices Rise While Chili and Shallot Prices Fall
medium.summary: Based on the National Strategic Food Price Information Center (PIHPS) data for July 5, 2026, red cayenne pepper prices fell sharply by 7.93% to Rp 62,100/kg and large red chili dropped 5.51% to Rp 50,500/kg, while medium shallots declined 6% to Rp 47,800/kg. In contrast, meat and rice prices moved upward, with garlic edging up 0.92% to Rp 44,100/kg. Mixed food commodity price movements are relevant to inflation monitoring and purchasing power assessments for Indonesian businesses and consumers.

medium.title: 200 Rural Banks (BPR/BPRS) Queue Up for Merger Approval — Here Are the Details
medium.summary: As of June 2026, 200 People's Economy Banks (BPR) and Sharia People's Economy Banks (BPRS) are currently in the merger and consolidation approval process at the Financial Services Authority (OJK), while 81 have already been approved to consolidate into 24 entities. OJK's Head of Banking Supervision, Dian Ediana Rae, stated this consolidation is part of a national banking strengthening policy under POJK Number 7 of 2024. This ongoing consolidation wave is reshaping Indonesia's rural banking landscape and may present both risks and opportunities for stakeholders in the sector.
